sections.title: Four variables that determine your AI automation cost
sections.description: Understanding these drivers helps you budget realistically and scope the right project for your needs.

items.title: 1. Document Complexity & Format Variation
items.description: The single largest cost variable. Single-format, structured documents cost baseline. Multi-format (3–10 formats): +$8K–$20K. Highly varied (100+ formats, scanned, handwritten): +$20K–$50K. Real-time sync: +$10K–$25K.
items.label: Document Complexity

items.title: 2. System Integration Count & Depth
items.description: Each system the automation reads from or writes to adds scope. Read-only API: $3K–$8K. Write API (CRM/ERP): $6K–$15K. SAP integration: $8K–$20K. Legacy (no API): $10K–$30K.
items.label: Integration Scope

items.title: 3. Exception Handling & Human Review Workflow
items.description: Exception routing infrastructure separates production automation from a prototype. Building the exception handling workflow adds $8,000–$25,000 but is essential for reliable production deployment.
items.label: Exception Management

items.title: 4. Straight-Through Processing Rate Target
items.description: The percentage of documents processed without human intervention. 50–65% STP: baseline. 70–80% STP: +$10K–$25K. 85%+ STP: +$25K–$60K for comprehensive edge case handling.
items.label: Accuracy Target

sections.title: ROI reference: when AI automation pays for itself
sections.description: The most important cost question isn't 'how much does automation cost?' — it's 'what is this automation worth?'

blocks.heading: Invoice processing automation ($25,000–$55,000)
paragraphs: Manual processing cost: $15–$35 per invoice × 5,000 invoices/month = $75,000–$175,000/year.
AI automation: $2–$6 per invoice + $1,500/month operating = $24,000–$36,000 + $18,000/year operating.

blocks.heading: Email/ticket routing automation ($20,000–$50,000)
paragraphs: AI routing at 70% deflection rate + 30% human review: $18,000/year operating.

blocks.heading: Compliance document screening ($35,000–$85,000)
paragraphs: Compliance analyst at $80,000/year reviewing 10,000 documents/month manually.
AI screening reduces review to 15% of documents: ~65% analyst time saved = ~$52,000/year labor reduction.

sections.title: AI automation vs. traditional RPA: which is cheaper?
sections.description: For fixed-format, deterministic workflows, RPA may be cheaper. For variable formats, AI automation delivers lower total cost of ownership over 3 years.

blocks.heading: Cost comparison table
paragraphs: **Maintenance cost:** Traditional RPA: High (breaks on format change) | AI Automation: Lower (adapts to variation)
**Capability (structured, fixed format):** Traditional RPA: Excellent | AI Automation: Good
**Capability (unstructured, variable):** Traditional RPA: None | AI Automation: Excellent
**Exception rate (real-world documents):** Traditional RPA: 30–50% | AI Automation: 10–25%
**3-year TCO (variable format workflows):** Traditional RPA: Higher (frequent rebuild) | AI Automation: Lower (adapts without rebuild)

blocks.heading: Bottom line
paragraphs: For fixed-format, deterministic workflows, traditional RPA may be cheaper. For workflows with document format variation, natural language, or judgment requirements, AI automation delivers lower total cost of ownership over 3 years despite higher upfront cost.

sections.title: The questions serious buyers ask before committing to AI automation
sections.description: No vague promises and no hidden discovery call required to understand the fundamentals.

items.objection: Traditional RPA is cheaper — why go with AI automation?
items.answer: Traditional RPA is cheaper for fixed-format, deterministic workflows. When your documents come in variable formats, contain natural language requiring interpretation, or involve decisions beyond explicit rules, RPA produces unacceptable exception rates. ClickMasters honestly evaluates which approach is right for your specific workflow.

items.objection: How much does AI automation cost?
items.answer: $15,000–$400,000 depending on workflow complexity and integration scope. Most single-workflow automation projects run $20,000–$75,000.

items.objection: How long does AI automation implementation take?
items.answer: Single workflow: 6–14 weeks. Enterprise multi-workflow platform: 18–36 weeks.

items.objection: What straight-through processing rate can we realistically achieve?
items.answer: Depends on your document quality and complexity — ClickMasters sets realistic STP targets based on sample document assessment during Discovery, not aspirational marketing claims.

sections.title: Questions about AI automation cost and scope
sections.description: Clear technical and commercial answers before you start.

items.question: What's the minimum budget for AI automation that delivers meaningful ROI?
items.answer: $15,000–$25,000 for a focused single-workflow automation (invoice processing, email triage, simple document extraction) where the labor cost avoided makes the investment clearly worthwhile.

items.question: Can AI automation integrate with our existing RPA tools (UiPath, Automation Anywhere)?
items.answer: Yes — AI automation complements existing RPA by handling the document understanding and classification steps that RPA can't do, with RPA continuing to handle the downstream structured workflow steps.

items.question: How do we measure whether AI automation is working?
items.answer: Through straight-through processing rate, cost per document processed, exception rate by document type, and processing cycle time — ClickMasters builds these metrics into every automation deployment.

items.question: How long does AI automation development take?
items.answer: 6–36 weeks depending on scope. Single workflow: 6–14 weeks. Enterprise platform: 18–36 weeks.

items.question: Does AI automation require changes to our existing systems?
items.answer: ClickMasters designs automation as an integration layer that works with your existing systems via API — typically not requiring system replacement or significant workflow redesign.

items.question: What happens when a new document format appears that the system hasn't seen?
items.answer: New formats are routed to exception handling for human processing and model feedback — ClickMasters builds the feedback loop that allows the model to learn from exceptions and reduce exception rates over time.

items.question: What's the difference between AI automation and traditional RPA?
items.answer: RPA follows explicit rules on structured inputs — it breaks when formats change. AI automation understands document content and adapts to variation — better for unstructured data, natural language, and judgment-based decisions. ClickMasters evaluates which approach is appropriate for your specific workflow.

items.question: Does ClickMasters offer fixed-price AI automation contracts?
items.answer: Yes — fixed-price automation projects are standard. We scope the workflow during Discovery and deliver at the agreed fixed price, with no cost surprises from scope creep on defined requirements.

sections.title: ClickMasters publishes AI automation pricing when competitors don't

blocks.heading: Zero of the major automation agencies publish their pricing
paragraphs: Almost every AI automation agency requires a sales conversation before disclosing even a rough cost estimate. This opacity makes it difficult for buyers to budget realistically or compare options before investing time in multiple conversations.

ClickMasters publishes detailed pricing by workflow type because automation scope is genuinely estimable by engineers who have built enough of these systems to know what drives cost—document complexity, integration scope, exception handling, and STP targets—and because pricing transparency lets you walk into a Discovery call already informed about what a fair price actually looks like.
